title: Pulling Up Seedlings to Help Them Grow
text:
Mencius told this story to explain how a person should cultivate character, and it has been repeated in China ever since.

There was a man of Song who was worried that the young shoots of his grain were not growing fast enough. Every day he went out to the field to look at them, and every day they seemed no taller. At last he could not stand it any longer. He went into the field and, one by one, pulled each seedling up a little, to make it taller.

He came home in the evening completely exhausted and told his family that he was worn out, because he had spent the whole day helping the seedlings grow. His son, alarmed, ran out to the field to look. All the seedlings had withered.

Mencius drew the lesson himself. Few people in the world, he said, do not try to help their seedlings grow this way. Some think nothing can be done and neglect them, never bothering to weed. Others try to force them, pulling them up. Neglecting does no good, but forcing does positive harm.
lesson: Growth in people, skills and projects needs steady care, not force. Pushing for results before their time can kill what you are trying to help.
people: A man of Song, his son, Mencius
